headline: Nearly 1 billion barrels drained from global oil inventories since Hormuz disruption
dek: Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, nearly 1 billion barrels have been drained from global oil inventories ('The world has eroded its supply buffers'). Diesel stocks in some markets are at 35-year seasonal lows; other markets face a 600 billion cubic…
sources: Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber, ADNOC CEO, opening address at ADIPEC 2026, Abu Dhabi (via Reuters)
fault_line: Who pays for the war: households at the pump vs the 'small price' for crippling Tehran -- the pocketbook frame vs the security frame.

sections.what_happened: Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, nearly 1 billion barrels have been drained from global oil inventories ('The world has eroded its supply buffers'). Diesel stocks in some markets are at 35-year seasonal lows; other markets face a 600 billion cubic feet LNG supply gap; shipping/logistics now exceed 30% of the cost of a barrel vs under 5% before the war; Brent ~$110, ~50% above February pre-war levels. IEA agreed in October to release 20m+ barrels of diesel; Aramco's Nasser said last month fewer than 6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain, mostly not practically available.
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire (primary carrier) + The National own ADIPEC reporting + Upstream; Hindu BusinessLine/Devdiscourse/Profit/LBC are Reuters syndication, same family, not additional corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: None against the speech itself; the 1-billion-barrel figure is the CEO's aggregate claim, not an independently audited inventory count, and no methodology was published with the speech. PortWatch gap: newest snapshot (portwatch-2026-10-26.json) is STALE (observation 2026-10-18) -- no fresh counted Hormuz transit figure is rendered alongside this item.
sections.why_matters: Hard counted number + pocketbook frame: '1 BILLION barrels gone -- and diesel at a 35-year low.' Proven-set energy lane; lead with what it costs the viewer, not the conference.
